title: Tensor product of explicit divisor modules realizes addition
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C$ a smooth connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], with structure morphism $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For any two divisors $A,B$ [def-sc-divisor], their valuation-bounded modules satisfy $\mathcal O_C(A)\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal O_C(B)\cong\mathcal O_C(A+B)$, with tensor product as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No properness or effectiveness is assumed.

source.place: Proof, homomorphism assertion: multiplication of rational sections; compare Stacks Divisors Tag 02SL.

proof.text: For sections s of O(A) and t of O(B) on an open V, take pointwise product st. It is locally constant. At a closed point either a factor is zero, or additivity of the order gives ord(st)+A(P)+B(P)=(ord(s)+A(P))+(ord(t)+B(P))>=0. Pointwise multiplication is bilinear over the regular-section scalar action and commutes with restriction. The universal property of the sheafified tensor product induces O(A) tensor O(B) to O(A+B).

Choose a uniformizer t at a closed point P. Apply lem-sc-divisor-module-local to A, B and A+B with this same t and intersect the three neighbourhoods. On their intersection the source factors have generators t^(-A(P)) and t^(-B(P)) and the target has generator t^(-A(P)-B(P)). The product morphism becomes O tensor O to O, the monoidal unit multiplication, which is an isomorphism.

These neighbourhoods cover all closed points and also the generic point, since every nonempty open contains it and a closed point exists. Every point is closed or generic by lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings. The local inverses agree on overlaps as inverses of the same multiplication morphism, so they glue to its global inverse by the sheaf property. This gives the stated nonempty isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of the multiplication-isomorphism step in lem-sc-divisor-toPic-representative; Stacks 02SL supplies valuation additivity.

mathlib_searches.query: Tensor product of modules associated to divisors is the module of the sum
The sheaf associated to a divisor on a smooth curve respects addition by tensor product
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, including Proj.add_apply and elliptic-curve ideal class identities; none states the explicit scheme divisor-module tensor comparison.

msearch grep found no hits. Direct rg on Sheaf found only DivisorModule, DivisorModuleLocal, DivisorLineBundleAgreesSC and the representative/class comparison. Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry/Modules has no divisor construction; ring-level PicardGroup is not this sheaf statement.

from.place: Proof, homomorphism assertion: multiplication identifies O(A) tensor O(B) with O(A+B).

lean.statement: theorem Divisor.nonempty_module_tensor_add_iso (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] (A B : C.Divisor) : Nonempty (A.moduleOfSmoothConnectedCurve k C f ⊗ B.moduleOfSmoothConnectedCurve k C f ≅ (A + B).moduleOfSmoothConnectedCurve k C f)
